scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The origin of Danza de la Botella remains unclear, but one theory suggests it derived from the galopa folk dance, which involved dancers balancing jugs on their heads.
Over time, glass bottles replaced the jugs, evolving into the current form of the dance.
on_screen: Map: Paraguay · South America
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is a folk tradition performed in cultural celebrations and has gained visibility through popular media such as The Amazing Race and Got Talent España.
It showcases balance, grace, and Paraguayan cultural identity.
on_screen: Footage — MISSING (use images)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Female dancers wear ankle-length skirts and balance glass bottles on their heads while dancing to Paraguayan polka music.
Movements are mostly improvised, with dancers holding the ruffles of their skirts with outstretched arms to maintain balance and the illusion of no bottles.
The dance can be performed solo, in pairs, or groups.
Watch for Bottle stacking.

No regional variants are described in the sources.
